title: Correctness and Stability of a Radix Pass
statement: Let a resource-limited program have procedures at positions $pc$ and $pp$ containing the counting-sort and copy routines, respectively. Let $A$ describe a radix pass on $w$ indices stored from address $perm$, with keys $kd(i)$ at addresses $key+i\,stride+off$, all below $nb$; let $\pi$ be a permutation list of these indices, and let $\mu$ be the initial memory. Assume $\pi$ has length $w$, all its entries are below $w$, it is stored at $perm$, each key cell contains $kd(i)<nb$, the key cells precede $perm$, the counters start at $cnt$ after the index and scratch regions, the counter region of length $nb+1$ lies within the $R$ cells from $perm$, and $perm+R$ is within the space limit; also assume the space limit is at most the word bound. Suppose the input variables give $w$, $perm$, $key$, $stride$, $off$, $nb$, and $cnt$ safely, the recursion depth is below the depth limit, and $84w+58nb+72$ plus the costs of those five expressions is at most $T$. Then the radix-pass program has an execution of cost at most $T$ after which only the designated unused variable may have changed, all memory outside the $R$ cells from $perm$ is unchanged, each counter at $cnt+t$ for $t\le nb$ equals the number of indices $i<w$ with $kd(\pi_i)<t$, and the indices stored from $perm$ form a stable permutation of $\pi$ ordered by nondecreasing $kd$ values.
